channels.label: New photographs and a rewritten profile
channels.rationale: Listing quality is the cheapest lever a shelter controls.
channels.evidence_detail: Not measurable in this dataset. Austin's public export contains no photograph or listing field, so we cannot estimate the effect and do not claim one.

channels.label: Place in a foster home
channels.rationale: Foster placement precedes adoption for a large share of Austin adoptions, especially for neonates.
channels.evidence_detail: 12,175 of 62,130 adoptions in this dataset carry the Foster outcome subtype, and neonates reach 47.8 percent cumulative adoption incidence by day 90 against 21.4 percent by day 30, a pattern consistent with a foster then adopt pathway.

channels.label: Feature at a weekend adoption event
channels.rationale: Puts the animal in front of walk-in traffic it would not otherwise see.
channels.evidence_detail: Event participation is not recorded in the public export.

channels.label: Medical or behaviour intervention
channels.rationale: Intake condition is one of the strongest measured predictors of a slow exit.
channels.evidence_detail: Animals arriving injured reach 18.5 percent 30-day adoption against 43.4 percent for animals arriving in normal condition, and the Cox hazard ratio for injured intake is 0.477.

channels.label: Senior-focused outreach
channels.rationale: Senior animals are the slowest life stage in this dataset.
channels.evidence_detail: Seniors reach 17.8 percent cumulative adoption incidence by day 30 against 59.8 percent for puppies and kittens; the Cox hazard ratio for the senior band is 0.425.

channels.label: Feature on social channels
channels.rationale: Extends reach beyond walk-in traffic at near zero marginal cost.
channels.evidence_detail: No reach or referral data is available in the public export.
